title: Stage 3 — JavaScript & the DOM
goal: Build interactive CRUD on mock data in the browser — debug with DevTools Elements and Console.
summary: Selectors, events, dynamic UI, mock data. The screen behaves like an app before any server exists.

checkpoint.prompt: Your list looks wrong but `console.log(workouts)` shows the right count. Where is the bug?

choices.text: The render function — data is fine, DOM wasn't updated correctly

checkpoint.explanation: Console confirms data; Elements shows DOM. If they disagree, fix render.

checkpoint.prompt: JavaScript changes what the user sees by updating…

choices.text: The DOM — the browser's live representation of the page

checkpoint.explanation: The DOM is the tree of elements the browser renders. Your JS reads and updates it.

checkpoint.prompt: A form's submit button is clicked. What should happen first in your code?

choices.text: Prevent the default page reload and run your handler

checkpoint.explanation: `event.preventDefault()` stops the browser refresh so your JavaScript controls what happens.

checkpoint.prompt: User adds an item to your mock array. The list on screen is stale. Fix?

choices.text: Re-run your render function so the DOM reflects the array
Ask the user to manually refresh the browser every time
Add a second array that never updates

checkpoint.explanation: When data changes, re-render (or update the DOM). That's the core UI loop.

checkpoint.prompt: Good structure: one function loads/updates data, another renders HTML. Why?

choices.text: Later you swap mock data for fetch() without rewriting the whole UI

checkpoint.explanation: Separating data access from rendering is what makes Stage 6's API hookup a small change.

checklist.label: Mock data array with sample records
`renderWorkouts()` updates the DOM from the array
Form adds a new item to mock data and re-renders the list
Empty state when the list has zero items
Verified behavior in DevTools Elements and Console

questions.prompt: What is the Console tab best for in this stage?

choices.text: Reading errors and logging values while debugging JavaScript

questions.explanation: Console shows errors and lets you inspect data while building DOM logic.

questions.prompt: After changing a JavaScript array, why might the page still look wrong?

choices.text: The DOM wasn't updated to reflect the new data

questions.explanation: Data and display are separate — you must re-render or patch the DOM when data changes.

questions.prompt: What does `event.preventDefault()` on a form submit do?

choices.text: Stops the browser's default full-page reload

questions.explanation: Without it, the page reloads and your JavaScript state is lost.

questions.prompt: Why use mock data before building an API?

choices.text: You can design and test the UI independently
Mock data is required for production

questions.explanation: Building the screen first separates UI problems from network and server problems.

choices.text: The first DOM element with id="workout-list"
All workout records from the database

questions.explanation: querySelector finds one element in the live DOM tree by CSS selector.
